title: Publish the Go module with prebuilt native artifacts
description:
nano-rspow-go is a source checkout only. Its README states that prebuilt Go module publishing is a separate release task, and the module cannot be consumed with a plain go get because the native library has to be built locally first.

Deliver:
- a published module that resolves the native library per target through the normal cgo target variables
- one native artifact set per target from the same matrix as the CLI release (macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux arm64/x86_64, Windows x86_64), with SHA-256 checksums
- the header published alongside them
- a release note recording the Rust crate version and the ABI version reported by nano_rspow_abi_version()
- verification that go get plus a known-vector generation and validation test works on each target

Measure cgo overhead separately from PoW throughput, as TODO-local-work.md requires.

title: Add HTTP contract tests for the work server
description:
nano-rspow-cli/src/server.rs has unit tests for the RPC dispatch, but nano-rspow-cli/tests/cli_tests.rs has no coverage of the serve subcommand at all. TODO-local-work.md asks for HTTP contract tests for every action: work_generate, work_cancel, work_validate, status, and benchmark.

Bind the server to an ephemeral port, POST each action, and assert the response shape, including the failure modes: malformed hash, malformed work value, malformed threshold, unknown action, cancellation of an in-flight request, and a duplicate hash while one is already queued.

The same list also asks for a Nano known-vector client fixture that exercises the full request flow.

title: Publish CLI binaries for five platforms with SHA-256 checksums
description:
TODO-local-work.md requires tagged-release archives for macOS x64/ARM64, Linux x64/ARM64, and Windows x64, published with SHA-256 checksums. Nothing in .github/workflows produces a binary today: cargo-publish ships the nano-rspow-cli crate to crates.io, and the node, python, and web workflows publish their own packages.

Add a release workflow triggered on version tags that:
- builds the nano-rspow binary for the five targets
- publishes one archive per target with a SHA-256 checksum beside it
- records the Rust version and the work-server ABI version in the release notes

This is the artifact baseline both the work-peer story and the Go module matrix depend on.

title: Test the Go bindings against the native engine in CI
description:
The Go module had no CI. nano-rspow-ffi was only ever compiled as part of another crate's build, and the Go tests only ran by hand on a machine that already had the native library built.

Add .github/workflows/go-tests.yml running on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest:
- cargo build -p nano-rspow-ffi (default features, so the shipped wgpu configuration is what gets built)
- gofmt check and go vet
- CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./...
- a smoke test of the streaming CLI at the dev threshold

Both runners matter: the cgo directives link different system libraries per platform, so a native boundary change can break one platform's link while the other still passes.

title: Gate Rust changes on fmt, clippy, and tests in CI
description:
No CI workflow compiled and tested the Rust workspace on a pull request. The publish workflows build the crates and the browser workflow exercises the WebAssembly path, but the core crate, the CLI, the FFI crate, and the Go-facing headers were only ever compiled as a side effect of another crate's build.

Add .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml running, on ubuntu-latest with a pinned toolchain:
- cargo fmt --all --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo test --workspace --exclude nano-rspow-python
- cargo check -p nano-rspow-python --all-targets

The Python binding is excluded from cargo test because it is a cdylib built against pyo3/extension-module, which does not link libpython: macOS tolerates the undefined symbols and Linux does not.
close_reason: Done in 41e1572: .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml gates fmt, clippy, and tests on a pinned 1.98.0 toolchain; the Python binding is checked rather than tested for the pyo3 linking reason. A rustfmt sweep landed first in daaf0c8.

title: Close out the rsnano head-to-head experiment
description:
experiment/rsnano-head-to-head holds one unmerged commit that adds nano-rspow-rsnano, a port of the rsnano-node work crate, so the CPU and OpenCL work pools can race against ours in the CLI benchmark. It was used to derive the pre-spun CPU thread pool plan, and nothing has run it since.

Decide one way and record it:
- fold it into the CLI benchmark behind an optional cargo feature, so the comparison stays reproducible, or
- archive it and file the numbers in PERFORMANCE_BENCHMARK.md, which is the only surface where numbers belong, then delete the branch

Either way, state which surface produced each number: the core CLI is the only one whose results may be filed.

title: Share one Nano known-vector fixture across every binding
description:
Known vectors are duplicated per binding: the Python tests carry one, the Go tests carry another, and the Rust side has its own in-crate constants. Every binding can therefore drift independently while still passing its own suite.

Publish one fixture (hash, expected work value, expected difficulty, and the threshold that makes it valid) and consume it from the Rust core, the CLI, the FFI crate, the Go module, the Node addon, the Python binding, and the web binding. The Go binding already asserts the native ABI version at generator creation, so the same discipline applies to the vectors.

title: Prune stale local branches and worktrees
description:
The repository carried six local branches that were either merged into main or superseded, plus three worktree registrations, two of which pointed at deleted directories in /private/tmp.

Removed: agent/go-bindings, agent/work-peer, benchmark/native-bridge, docs/api-reference-refresh, feat/browser-pow-recommendation, feat/cpu-pre-spun-pool, the worktrees/browser-pow-recommendation worktree, and the two stale /private/tmp worktree registrations.

Kept on purpose because they hold commits main does not have: competitor/nano-pow, experiment/gen6-hd3000-pow, experiment/rsnano-head-to-head. Remote branches were left untouched.
